haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 after the Key Service lookup fails. Redis is not touched, so no rate-limit counter is affected.
haiku-low.q2: 100 per minute in total for Standard, since the budget is shared by all of the customer's keys.
haiku-low.q3: A 429 with Retry-After only. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. Rejected requests are not incremented, so 429s use no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. An allowed request counts against the budget even when the backend returns 500.
haiku-low.q6: It fails open: the request is forwarded anyway, with no X-RateLimit headers, and the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric is emitted.
haiku-low.q7: Standard is 100 requests per minute. Enterprise is not decided yet.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis, under key rl:{customerId}:{minute}. Keys expire after 120 seconds, which removes old minutes.
haiku-low.q9: The budget resets at the start of each clock minute, from the Redis server clock. Fixed windows, so the count starts fresh.
haiku-low.q10: The check_and_incr Lua script runs atomically in Redis, so requests from different instances cannot overshoot the limit.
haiku-low.q11: It is the seconds left until the current minute ends, from the Redis server clock, with a minimum of 1.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED for retries. The client gets no X-RateLimit headers and no rate-limit information on that response.

sonnet.q1: Gateway replies 401 and Redis is not touched, so no rate-limit counter is affected.
sonnet.q2: Budget is per customer, shared by all their keys, so 100 requests per minute total on Standard (Enterprise limit not decided).
sonnet.q3: A 429 with a Retry-After header (only that header). The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
sonnet.q4: No. The script rejects without incrementing, so 429s use no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. An allowed request counts even if the backend returns 500.
sonnet.q6: Fail open: the gateway forwards the request to the backend anyway, returns the response without X-RateLimit headers, and emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric.
sonnet.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise is not decided yet (open question).
sonnet.q8: In Redis, under the key rl:{customerId}:{minute}. The key expires after 120 seconds, which only cleans up old minutes.
sonnet.q9: At the start of each fixed clock minute (per the Redis server clock), the budget resets; a new minute uses a new key.
sonnet.q10: The check_and_incr Lua script runs atomically in Redis, so requests from different instances cannot overshoot the limit.
sonnet.q11: It is the seconds left in the current minute (window end), with a minimum of 1; Redis returns the seconds until window end on rejection.
sonnet.q12: Retry is NOT STATED. The 50 ms is a timeout on the Redis call and the request is forwarded anyway. The client gets the backend response with no X-RateLimit headers.
